subject: Architecture
title: Fire Safety: Lessons Written in Tragedy
description: A 1-minute de-risking session on Fire Safety: Lessons Written in Tragedy.

hook.text: Skyscraper fire codes exist because people died. Every rule has a story behind it.

buildup.text: Stairwells must be pressurized, fire doors self-closing, and sprinklers on every floor.

discovery.text: Fireproofing coats every steel beam — steel loses half its strength at 1,100°F, well within fire range.

twist.text: The Grenfell Tower fire in 2017 revealed that cladding materials could spread flames up a building's exterior.

climax.text: After Grenfell, countries worldwide banned combustible cladding and rechecked thousands of buildings.

punchline.text: Every fire code is a memorial. The rules exist because something failed.

quiz.question: At what temperature does steel lose half its structural strength?

details.summary: Skyscraper fire safety evolved through disasters — from the 1911 Triangle Shirtwaist Factory fire to the 2017 Grenfell Tower tragedy. Modern codes require fire-resistant structural steel, pressurized stairwells, sprinkler systems.
details.whyItMatters: Every major advance in fire safety was written in response to lives lost. These tragedies drove building codes that save thousands of lives annually, making fire safety the most regulation-driven aspect of tall building design.
takeaways: Major fires drove building code improvements worldwide
Modern codes require sprinklers, pressurized stairs, and fire-rated materials
The Grenfell tragedy highlighted cladding safety failures

faq.question: What changed after the Grenfell Tower fire?
faq.answer: The 2017 fire killed 72 people when flames spread rapidly via combustible aluminum composite cladding. Countries worldwide banned or restricted similar cladding and launched remediation programs to replace it on existing buildings. Testing standards for facade fire performance were strengthened.

faq.question: How do skyscrapers prevent fire from spreading between floors?
faq.answer: Fire-rated floor assemblies, firestopping at slab edges, compartmentalization, sprinkler systems, and pressurized stairwells all contain fires to their floor of origin. Modern skyscrapers are designed so occupants above a fire can shelter safely while floors below evacuate.
